newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady, quiet in pre-weekend mood.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady, quiet in pre-weekend mood.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market held steady on Friday amid thin talk ahead of the weekend.
Traders said a lack of fresh buying support might depress sentiment next week.
Late Friday, a major was heard offering a 20,000-tonne cargo of the 180-cst grade for late June/early July delivery but there was no buyer.
"Demand seems pretty slack at the moment. There is not much direction," said one trader.

The market is waiting for results of a tender by Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent fuel oil for lifting in the the first half of July, traders said.
The tender will close on Tuesday and is valid for two days.
Fuel oil swaps also weakened along with overnight crude losses. June swaps were at $100.00/$100.75 against Thursday's $100.50/$101.25 and July swaps slipped to $99.00/$99.50 from $99.00/$99.75.
At least five cargoes sailing eastward from the Mediterranean and the Middle East are expected to arrive in mid-June and traders differed in views.
Some said the cargoes would fill up seasonally tight supplies in the summer while others said the cargoes were still seeking buyers, which might put prices under pressure.
However, they agreed that the $100.00-per-tonne level would be a strong support for the 180-cst grade.
Trading volume on the SIMEX fuel oil futures contract improved, with at least 60 100-tonne lots traded late on Friday.
July contract was traded 20 cents down to $99.80 and August was at $99.50.
